comparison.query: Compare the magnitude of mean symmetry to other features like mean radius, mean texture, and mean concavity in terms of their typical ranges and clinical relevance to tumor classification.

result.explanation: Mean symmetry is a dimensionless feature that measures the uniformity of tumor shape and is often considered clinically relevant in breast cancer classification. In the dataset, mean symmetry has a value of 0.1848, which falls within a typical range of 0.1 to 0.3 for benign tumors. Compared to mean radius (13.66), which is in a much larger scale (typically 10–30), and mean texture (19.13), which reflects surface irregularity and is highly correlated with malignancy, mean symmetry has a smaller magnitude but still contributes meaningfully to shape-based classification. Mean concavity (0.09657) is also in a similar range to symmetry and reflects irregularity, but symmetry is more directly tied to structural regularity. While not the most dominant feature in magnitude, mean symmetry shows moderate clinical relevance and is statistically significant in distinguishing benign from malignant tumors, especially when combined with other shape-related features. Masking this feature may reduce prediction confidence, particularly in models sensitive to shape regularity.
